title: One holy catholic church
hookLine: small c: universal; every tradition says it in its own sense

cards: Sunday morning, a Methodist church. The congregation stands to say the Apostles' Creed, and comes to a line that makes some visitors blink: I believe in the holy catholic church. Catholic?
Aren't we Methodists? Across town, at a Catholic parish, people are saying almost the same words. At the Orthodox church down the road, they say: one holy catholic and apostolic church.
Everyone is saying catholic. Not everyone means the same thing by it. Today's word is small c catholic, and it's bigger than any one church's name.

teach.h: KATH' HOLOU: ACCORDING TO THE WHOLE.
teach.b: Catholic comes from the Greek katholikos, from kath' holou: according to the whole. Whole, entire, universal.
Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, wrote letters on his way to martyrdom in Rome, so tradition says, and in one he puts it, roughly: wherever Jesus Christ is, there is the catholic church.
The whole church, not just one local gathering. Later, Cyril, bishop of Jerusalem, explained it to people preparing for baptism.

The church is catholic, he said, because it spreads through the whole world; because it teaches the whole faith; because it gathers every kind of person, rulers and ruled, learned and unlearned; and because it heals every kind of sin.
A monk, Vincent of Lérins, gave a test in Latin: quod ubique, quod semper, quod ab omnibus creditum est.
What has been believed everywhere, always, by everyone.
Today each church says catholic in its own sense.

teach.h: ONE HOLY CATHOLIC AND APOSTOLIC CHURCH.
teach.b: Roman Catholics mean the church in communion with the pope, where they believe the fullness of the church is found. Orthodox Christians mean the fullness of faith present in each local church gathered around its bishop.

In Protestant usage, it means the universal church of all believers, in every place and time, whatever their denomination. Luther's German catechism even says Christian church instead, to make that meaning plain.
They differ on what the word points to. But Cyril's reasons still sit under each of them: a church that isn't only for one country, one class, or one kind of person.

how: Christians across the churches say "one holy catholic and apostolic church" in the Nicene Creed or "the holy catholic church" in the Apostles' Creed, each understanding the word in their own tradition's sense.

games.q: you're Cyril, teaching people about to be baptized in Jerusalem. someone asks: why do we call the church catholic?
o: because it is ruled from one city.
because it spreads through the whole world, teaches the whole faith and gathers every kind of person.
games.why: Cyril gave several reasons: the whole world, the whole faith, every kind of person, healing every kind of sin.

practice: Picture the church nearest you, any church, the one you pass on the way to work or the one you grew up in: its doors, its people on a Sunday.
Then widen the picture to every church on your street, in your town, in your country, around the world, every kind of person.
If you pray, pray for that one local church and, through it, for the whole; if you don't, just hold the picture: one little building, and the whole wide world.

wordCard.voice: Catholic. Small c: from the Greek for according to the whole. Universal: the whole church, everywhere, every kind of person.

orig.note: Greek: universal, from kath' holou, according to the whole.
